solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Self-assembly bed with special base (10)

indicatorNotes.Self-assembly: flat-pack furniture comes in pieces you put together yourself, so the letters that follow arrive loose and must be built into a new order

annotation.surface: A flat-pack bed arrives with a special base to screw together.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes base a furniture part; here it is the adjective meaning low or contemptible.
annotation.definitionFit: Base conduct is mean and contemptible, which is what despicable means.

entries.clue: Avoid love in the Midlands (4)

blocks.note: to dodge, as when you lower your head to miss a blow
the everyday term of endearment in the English Midlands, used where others say 'love'

annotation.surface: Someone is advised to steer clear of romance in central England.
annotation.walkthrough: The Midlands are the central counties of England, around Nottingham and Birmingham, where people call each other 'duck' as others say 'love'.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses are everyday: dodging a blow by bobbing down, and the Midlands endearment, a regional use.

entries.clue: Plenty of dons ship specimens (7)

indicatorNotes.dons: to don is to put on, as clothing; the first piece puts the second on around itself

blocks.note: plenty of room is ample room

annotation.surface: Many Oxford dons are shipping off specimens.
annotation.walkthrough: Dons looks like the university teachers; it is the verb, with AMPLE wearing the ship's SS as a coat.
annotation.definitionFit: Samples are specimens taken to represent the whole.

entries.clue: One with new toilet trouble (13)

blocks.note: a public convenience is a British public toilet

annotation.surface: Someone has a problem with their newly fitted toilet.
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'public convenience' is a public toilet, so convenience alone can stand for toilet.
annotation.definitionFit: Trouble, as a noun for bother or difficulty, is an inconvenience.

entries.clue: Lather conceals these things (8)

blocks.note: soap foam covering things up; read the word itself, and L-A-THE-R hides two small words
the surface makes them any objects; the setter means the grammatical kind of word hidden there

annotation.surface: Soapy lather hides whatever is underneath it.
annotation.walkthrough: Look inside the word lather: L-A-THE-R holds A and THE, the two English articles. 'Things' is the everyday sense of articles too.
annotation.definitionFit: A and THE are the indefinite and definite articles, and both sit inside LATHER.

entries.clue: First in line heading for soup and rolls (5)

indicatorNotes.in: the first piece goes inside the second
indicatorNotes.heading: the head of each word is its first letter

blocks.note: the heads of line and soup
1st, with the digit written as I

annotation.surface: At a dinner, the person first in the queue heads for the soup and bread rolls.
annotation.walkthrough: Rolls in the surface are bread; here they are lists, as in the electoral roll or a roll call.
annotation.definitionFit: A roll is an official list of names, so rolls are lists.

entries.clue: Sign one’s expecting seat … lead in polls (4)

indicatorNotes.lead in: the lead of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: British slang for the backside, what one sits on

annotation.surface: An election story: a candidate's seat looks safe with a lead in the polls.
annotation.walkthrough: Seat and polls paint an election; seat is the bottom you sit on, and 'expecting' means pregnant.
annotation.definitionFit: A pregnant woman's bump is the visible sign that she is expecting.

entries.clue: What one might complete to get into Oxford flat (7)

annotation.definition: What one might complete to get into Oxford

blocks.clueFragment: What one might complete to get into Oxford

annotation.surface: An applicant fills in paperwork to win a place at Oxford and a room there.
annotation.walkthrough: The first half is a playful split: a uni form is the form you complete to get into a university. Flat is not an apartment but 'level, unvarying'.
annotation.definitionFit: Something flat, with no rises or variation, is uniform.

entries.clue: Anodyne murderer, supporter of Spooner (10)

indicatorNotes.of Spooner: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of pairs of words, so the two words just named swap their first sounds

blocks.note: Cain killed Abel, the first murderer in the Bible; his K sound goes to the second word
a pillar holds a roof up; it gives its P to the first word

annotation.surface: A dull killer turns out to be a supporter of Spooner.
annotation.walkthrough: Anodyne looks like 'bland' describing the murderer; as a noun it is a medicine that soothes pain.
annotation.definitionFit: An anodyne is a painkilling drug, which is what a painkiller is.

entries.clue: Funny business I see going on close to referendum (5)

indicatorNotes.close to: the close of a word is its last letter
indicatorNotes.going on: in an across clue, going on after something means written after it

blocks.note: I, then the letter C, whose name is 'see'

annotation.surface: Someone notices some shady goings-on as a referendum nears.
annotation.walkthrough: Funny business reads as one phrase meaning skulduggery; split it, and funny is the definition while business is CO.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: funny in the amusing sense, as a stand-up is a funny person.

entries.clue: Conductor contains high electric current (9)

indicatorNotes.high: high means drunk or intoxicated, so the letters are all over the place

blocks.note: I is the symbol for current in physics

annotation.surface: An electrical conductor carries a high-voltage current.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is physics, with a conductor carrying current; the conductor is a musician, and 'contains' is not a container signal but letters to mix.
annotation.definitionFit: Arturo Toscanini was a famous Italian orchestral conductor.

entries.clue: A big reduction changes the game (7,6)

indicatorNotes.changes: the letters before it change their order

annotation.surface: A huge price cut is a game-changer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Changes the game' reads as the business cliché, but changes is the anagram signal and the game is what the answer is.
annotation.definitionFit: Auction bridge is the card game that preceded contract bridge.

entries.clue: Upright type handily disclosing enemy position? (8,5)

annotation.definition: Upright type handily disclosing enemy position?

blocks.note: a person of good character in the surface; really a tall object that stands upright
sounds like a spy's tip-off; time is 'the enemy', and hands disclose where it stands

annotation.surface: A soldier discreetly signals where the enemy is, perhaps 'at twelve o'clock'.
annotation.walkthrough: In crosswords and in the proverb, time is 'the enemy'. A tall upright clock shows where the time is by its hands, hence 'handily'.
annotation.definitionFit: A longcase, or grandfather, clock stands upright and its hands show the position of time.

entries.clue: A possibly poor old bug needing treatment (5,5)

indicatorNotes.needing treatment: the letters before it need working on, so they are rearranged

annotation.surface: Some poor old insect, or a sick patient, needs care.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital A looks like the article; it is the blood type A, and 'possibly' marks it as one example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by 'possibly': A is one type of blood, alongside B, AB and O.

entries.clue: Re-enlist having been redrafted? Bugger! (8)

indicatorNotes.having been redrafted: to redraft is to rewrite, so the letters are set down in a new order

annotation.surface: A soldier swears on being drafted into the army all over again.
annotation.walkthrough: Bugger looks like the British swear word; it is one who bugs, planting hidden microphones.
annotation.definitionFit: A crossword-only sense: a bugger is one who plants bugs, hidden microphones, to eavesdrop.

entries.clue: Lousy M&S rolls stuffed in face (6)

indicatorNotes.rolls: turns over, so the letters run backwards
indicatorNotes.stuffed in: the first piece is packed inside the second

blocks.note: the initials, which roll over to SM

annotation.surface: Someone stuffs their face with some poor bread rolls from Marks & Spencer.
annotation.walkthrough: M&S is Marks & Spencer, a British high-street store. Rolls is not bread but the reversal signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Lousy work is poor, and dismal also means poor or depressing.

entries.clue: Half the clues here are so tired and gloomy (8)

blocks.clueFragment: Half the clues here are so
blocks.note: clues are either across or down, and this one is a down

annotation.surface: A solver admits half these clues have left them tired and low.
annotation.walkthrough: The puzzle itself supplies the first part: half its clues are Down clues.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a pessimistic, low-spirited mood.

entries.clue: Get thanks, having opened old booze store (6)

indicatorNotes.having opened: the first piece has opened up the second and got inside it

blocks.note: a wine bin, where bottles are racked

annotation.surface: Someone is thanked for opening the old off-licence.
annotation.walkthrough: TA is the British casual word for thanks.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to get a ticket is to acquire it.

entries.clue: Ultimately rampant cad, supporter of Napoleon (7)

indicatorNotes.Ultimately: at the last, so the word's final letter

blocks.note: old British slang for a scoundrel

annotation.surface: A wild scoundrel turns out to be a follower of Napoleon Bonaparte.
annotation.walkthrough: Napoleon is not the emperor but the pig who rules in Orwell's Animal Farm; a pig's foot supports it.
annotation.definitionFit: A trotter is a pig's foot, and Orwell's Napoleon is a pig, so it stands on trotters.

entries.clue: Hard parts done with accuracy on My Way (8)

indicatorNotes.parts: the first piece parts the second, splitting it to sit inside
indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, placed after what follows

blocks.note: a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'
a nice distinction is a fine, precise one

annotation.surface: Someone takes the tricky bits of Sinatra's My Way very precisely.
annotation.walkthrough: My Way looks like the song title; My is the exclamation COR, and Way the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A corniche is a coastal road along a cliff, so a way.

entries.clue: Record with cornet on that some men slap on? (7)

indicatorNotes.with: with the cornet on, the record wears it, so the second piece goes around the first

blocks.note: an ice-cream cornet is a cone

annotation.surface: A jazz record with cornet playing, of the kind some men love.
annotation.walkthrough: Cornet suggests a trumpet on a jazz record; in Britain an ice-cream cornet is the cone.
annotation.definitionFit: Cologne is scent that men splash on after shaving.

entries.clue: Long run doctor managed in Houston? (6,7)

indicatorNotes.managed: the letters before it are handled and worked into a new order

annotation.surface: A doctor ran a practice in Houston for many years.
annotation.walkthrough: Doctor looks like the anagram signal, but it is letters to mix; 'managed' does the rearranging. Astronauts address mission control simply as 'Houston'.
annotation.definitionFit: NASA's ground control is in Houston, and astronauts call it 'Houston', so the city's name stands for it.

entries.clue: Discontinue drug when patient comes around (5)

indicatorNotes.comes around: the second piece goes around the first

blocks.note: a doctor's patient is a case

annotation.surface: Doctors stop a drug once the patient comes round.
annotation.walkthrough: Comes around reads as regaining consciousness; it is the container signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to stop doing something.

entries.clue: Plastic bottles (only one left) (4)

indicatorNotes.bottles: the first word holds the answer inside it, as a bottle holds a drink

annotation.surface: Only one plastic bottle remains on the shelf.
annotation.walkthrough: Bottles looks like the noun; it is a verb, with plastic holding the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: the one remaining at the end of a line is the final one.

entries.clue: State where one might see hay withering (2,3,4)

indicatorNotes.State: to state is to say out loud, so the words are heard rather than read

blocks.note: a wain is a hay cart, as in Constable's painting The Hay Wain

annotation.surface: Somewhere you might see hay drying out.
annotation.walkthrough: State looks like a noun for condition; it is the verb. The Hay Wain is a famous English painting of a farm cart.
annotation.definitionFit: Something on the wane is declining, withering away.

entries.clue: A ministry u-turning over German doctrine (5)

indicatorNotes.u-turning: turning back, so the letters run the other way
indicatorNotes.over: the first piece goes over, around, the second

annotation.surface: A government ministry performs a U-turn over German policy.
annotation.walkthrough: MOD is Britain's Ministry of Defence.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a doctrine laid down as beyond question.

entries.clue: A grand company car? (4)

blocks.note: as in 'a pound a head', per head
a thousand, as in a salary of 50K

annotation.surface: A thousand pounds' worth of company car.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the company car as one example of a perk.
annotation.definitionFit: A company car is a classic perk, a job benefit beyond salary.

entries.clue: Treaty of Paris (earliest version)? (10)

blocks.note: Paris in its first form: a cluster of huts on an island in the Seine where the city began

annotation.surface: A historian asks about the first draft of the Treaty of Paris.
annotation.walkthrough: The Treaty of Paris looks like one title; split it, and Paris in its earliest form was a settlement.
annotation.definitionFit: A treaty is a settlement between parties, and a city begins as a settlement.
